item.content:encoded:
I think it's lacking a few key components as of now. I don't know how much you've already worked on it and if you are planning on including them already.

It says that the MTF Unit was sent and captured it, but it lacks explanation of how it was captured, nor is there information on how the SCP is contained in its cell, which I believe is a crucial piece in a SCP Article.
Aside from that, the portion you narrated regarding the surviving Doctor is a bit confusing, although comprehensible. However, I didn't understand how or why he wasn't attacked. Pardon if it's just my brain malfunctioning.

I think the idea would get better attention and have more chance of getting greenlights if the pitch is a bit more focused on the methods of containment and capture. Afterall, once you get your greenlights the narrative part of the idea will be completely up to you.

item.title: Re: SCP-5831 (greenlight needed)
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

My concern with this is that you haven't explained almost anything about your concept. You have 400 words to explain to us what you're trying to do with your story. What you have here is just a blurb of your story. What's the anomaly's motivation? What happened during the containment breaches? What are the ethical issues that this anomaly brings up to the Ethics Committee? How did the anomaly tried to free other SCPs?

Furthermore, you may want to read this essay about writing humanoid anomalies, or the 'Humanoids' tab in the HTWASCP page.

Overall, you need to explain more what are you planning to do with your story.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Weird/Horror SCP.

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP with multiple Incident Reports and connections to VII SCP's (for others or maybe for me to write).

Elevator Pitch: A Dishwasher that has tongues clean dishes within the SCP, if a human with a slightly above average IQ comes near the SCP they become hysterical, denying that the SCP is anomalous at all and inserts themselves into the SCP.

Central Narrative: This is suppose to be a weird SCP that has been Neutralized under the 05 command despite pleading from the Ethics committee. I make it a point that the Ethics committee points out that The SCP Foundation is not The DDD (Destroy, Destroy, Destroy) Foundation. The overall narrative is that the 05 are in a position of power and could abuse their power whenever and however they want. I'm hoping to make this multiple connections between SCP's.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook is more about how "unstable" the SCP is. Most foundation members (are assumed) to have a high IQ. This SCP doesn't allow high IQ's around it. The SCP is somewhat of a threat to the 05 command and is neutralized for that reason.

Additional Notes: I'm not anywhere near greenlights for the SCP. This was a very rough draft and if someone takes an interest in this SCP I would be glad to have someone possibly make this a joint venture. Thanks for future critiques.

item.title: Re: SCP Greenlight - The Marvelous Transformation Alchemy Machine
item.content:encoded:
Let's see what we have here.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

So my concern here is that this is just 294 but with alchemy. I think this machine would be too similar to 294 to be successful on its own. You have the spark of a story with the researcher creating a potentially dangerous substance, and I would suggest to expand upon that. What did they do? What were their motivations? What are they planning to do next?

As you mention, this machine would not be dangerous on its own, so you may as well create a story around it about how people misuse it. I still think it would be too similar to 294, but if you expand the alchemy thing, this will have a little more potential. Maybe instead of a 'modern' device, it would be better to do it as an 'ancient' one?

Overall, I think you need to add more story to this.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: Dr Cheese SCP idea.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: My design is meant to be spooky, but I may not achieve this factor.

Page Layout: The usual SCP statements, Item Name, Item Class but no picture. Information is going to be structured in the following layout; Appearance description (Height, weight, colour and shape), Discovery (How the anomaly was contained), Abilities (What the anomaly can do, how it does it etc) and the Addendums (Stories about previously explained things).

Elevator Pitch: The basic premise is a tall, slender, arctic hunter with elongated shoulder growths and large elbows, glowing crimson eyes, capable of seeing infrared radiation and heat signatures. This is used as a hunting technique in the arctic weather. The anomaly has thousands of tiny muscles on its skin capable of moving guanine crystals to adjust the wavelength of light being reflected off the skin of the anomaly. This is commonly known as camouflage, and is the same method that the Chamaeleonidae (Common Chameleon) uses. Bone marrow scans and nervous axon scans have suggested that overgrowths on the anomaly's shoulder blades and elbows contain many nerve endings, which transfer electrical signals in large amounts to a particular area which creates an electromagnetic field. These electromagnetic pulses disrupt nearby local electric signals. It may use this to alter the function of electrical signals in the brain, or to inhibit power of technology.

Central Narrative: The narrative for initial containment is the following: It was a normal day in the UK Arctic Research Facility. Cold, as usual, but the sacred electric heaters were keeping staff alive. It was collection day, where the scientific staff would take a collection of snow for carbon-testing, a process where the amount of carbon that is in a snowflake is collected to see the effects of the greenhouse effect. As the staff left the facility, the power went out. As the staff stumbled over to the generator, senior researcher Noel Leon noticed a small red glow. Must have been nothing. H got back to fixing the generator. The fuses had been replaced. They become brittle and break in the cold weather. But as soon as the generator start-up was initiated, the generator failed. What was going on? Suddenly, pat… pat… pat…. Something was behind him, but when he turned around, there was nothing but footprints. SNAP. The crunch of his bones in SCP-XXXX's mouth was horrifying, but unheard to remaining staff. As it entered the facility, seven of it's prey had already been frozen. An easy meal. Junior researcher Doctor Edward turned a corner, but the anomaly was gone, just a frozen, half-eaten corpse. The rest of the facility was wiped out, with the exception of Doctor Bradly was obliterated by SCP-XXXX. Doctor Bradly called local authorities and the foundation was alerted. MTF unit Delta-92 Snow-and-Tell was sent to the situation and captured the anomaly.

item.title: A Hilarious Trip Through Some of the Foundation's Most Infamous SCP's
item.content:encoded:
And their hair-brained attempts to kill what just won't stay dead.

I think at this point, the Foundation's attempt to torture and mutilate 682 has caused far more harm than good, and if there was even a cell of good in him (he seemed to like that one little girl)… Well, all that's left is a whole lot of hate.

And yet the more hair-brained the attempt, the more fun the read.

I'm hoping that there will continue to be even more hair-brained entries, and when ideas using SCPs runs out-and this is my over-imagination talking, I'd love to see him thrown in with characters from other universes.

We all know what would happen if 682 and someone like Vegeto were to be thrown into a fight together (682 would eventually adapt and become even more powerful, with the ability to launch blasts capable of destroying the planet), but I'd just love to read a showdown where his opponent apparently has him outmatched, and just keeps pushing his buttons, along the lines of Vegeto vs. Super Buu. I think 682 would throw death threats left and right, and curse like a drunk sailor! Probably in multiple languages.

In the meantime, I have plenty more termination entries to read, and this gem here!

leaves along time for things to kind of fade and become distant through reflection, hence Hector's coldness

This kind of gets to my emerging issue with the portrayal of robots/AI in this canon: that they're too human, or at least assumed to be. I feel like when you take something that is, at least practically, indistinguishable from a human, then give it perfect recall, or the ability to tell the future, or a complete absence of aging, you don't just get a human plus those things, but an entirely different experience.

To steal a line from Neil Postman, if you take an ecosystem and add caterpillars to it, you don't get that ecosystem with caterpillars; you get an entirely different ecosystem.

The AI's are presumably intended to evoke empathy through their resemblance to humans (and they do it quite well), but I can't help but feel that there's a lot of territory that could still be explored regarding what it is to be alive without falling back into the trope of anthropocentrism.

As for the tale itself, it's fine. I feel like so much has happened between reading the original tales and now that it's hard to feel all that much of a connection with the bot-soul. No voting for now.

item.title: Re: The Nanny
item.content:encoded:
I was thinking that it was a normal human nanny invited into a household to care for the family. However, the family were Sarkites and they performed a ritual to 'ascend' themselves and members of the household. The family had built an extensive set of tunnels beneath their house and when they performed the ritual they were put into pods undergoing a metamorphosis to become powerful entities. The rest of the staff of the house were transformed into horrifying entities all with different tasks, the nanny brings people to the pods, the cook prepares them for consumption by the family, the gardener maintains the tunnels in which they spawn their creatures and the butler feeds them by performing a ritual. I was also thinking that perhaps they have smaller entities called busyboys or handmaids which perform basic grunt work like tunnel digging as well as defence. The only 'non-monstrous' entity is the butler who through communication implies that perhaps he turned the family to sarkicism.

item.title: Re: Please read. (FROM AUTHOR)
item.content:encoded:
First off, I am new to this site, but I still want to give you critique.

+ Enter the critter cave
- Go back!

Object Class: KETER OH GOSH RUN

Keter means hard to contain, not dangerous. Also, you should not be putting this type of emotion in your writing. Have you ever written an informative essay? Would you put 'THE CHEETAH CAN RUN SUPER FAST DANGER!' in your writing? The answer is no, and it's even more emphasized on this site.

SCP-5188's cell door must be chained by 10 heavy padlocks, have a 5 digit access code, a level 4 card reader, and voice and oral recognition. NOBODY is allowed into SCP-5188's cage UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES (See incident 5188-A-1).

This contradicts itself. You say nobody is allowed in, but it has a level 4 card reader, and an access code. If the former is the current containment procedure, you should strike-through the other part to show it's not valid anymore.

It looks like a mother████ing cardboard spider.

You're writing a research paper, and you decided to put a swear word in your formal report. You need to use plain and professional tone; this is supposed to be a research document on a dangerous object, and you need to write the part.

SCP-5188 is a standard amazon box, with no anomalous effects. SCP-5188's anomalous affects only trigger when touched. When touched, SCP-5188 will suddenly sprout human arms and legs, through the bottom.

There's no narrative to this, and it seems like 'a thing that does a dangerous thing when x happens' cliché. Is there any research into why it does this or how it magically conjures up legs and arms?

SCP-5188 will then undergo a rage state, where it will kill everything in its path by [DATA EXPUNGED] them.

But.. why? I read this and came out feeling bored, because there's no plot or anything; just a dangerous thing which does not have any form of development.

Exactly 69 seconds (1 minute and 9 seconds) after a human is killed, more "cardboard spiders" drag them away.

Wait, how are more cardboard spiders coming out? I thought there was one box which sprouted legs and arms. Also, 69? Really?

therefore they are dubbed SCP-5188-1, and are to be treated as such.

The word choice here is suboptimal. You should say something such as, '(these entities are hereinafter referred to as SCP-5188-1.)'

INCIDENT-5188-A-1:

First off, before the incident, there was a Level 4 padlock. Level 4 clearance is rarely given out to administrative personnel, and even so, why would a Level 4 administrative personnel be in close proximity to a dangerous anomaly?

Dr. ███: THE ████? Is this normal? Ill write this down.

This is not normal human dialogue. A professional researcher wouldn't say this out loud.

Dr. ███: OH ████ ITS WEARING HIS FACE AND ITS ████ING SMILING AT ME! ITS ████ING SMILING! WHAT THE F-

I thought that he would've been prepared for the inevitable, since this was already written in the document before the test (I presume.)

SCP-5188 jumps through the glass and tackles Dr. ███. It then proceeds to
[DATA EXPUNGED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Huh? Why are there 3 redactions on 3 different lines? This makes no sense. Redactions =/= mystery value; only if they're done right. There's a good guide to redactions here.

Overall, this is a messy and rushed article, and I'm pretty sure this is a cold post as well. -1.

item.title: Worrisome Developments (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): The idea is to have a normal SCP document, but with periodic updates due to the the SCP growing out and developing.

Elevator Pitch: What initially started off as a finger has been growing slowly but surely more humanoid.

Central Narrative: A finger was handed over to the foundation. It moves entirely of its own accord and over time, grows outwards and generates more and more of the anatomy of a human. Alongside this growth is a rising intelligence and more complex behaviour. This will operate in a periodic update format with the most recent format showing entirely new behaviour to due the growth of the beginning of the head. I want to include experiments on the SCP as well but I can't think of that many off-hand.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP will hopefully work off of curiosity. It changes often and to a known set goal, while it isn't known why or how it is doing so.
